title: Melanzane alla Parmigiana
subtitle: Baked layers of aubergine, tomato sauce, and mozzarella
excerpt: Fried aubergine slices layered with tomato sauce, mozzarella, and parmesan, then baked until bubbling and golden. It takes time but almost all of it is hands-off.
sourceNotes: Southern Italian classic; associated with both Campania and Sicily. Salting the aubergine first draws out moisture and reduces oil absorption.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool completely, wrap well, and freeze for up to two months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat covered in a moderate oven.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Assemble in two dishes at the same time.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Parmigiana is best made a day ahead and reheated; the layers firm up and the flavour deepens.

content.text: Melanzane alla parmigiana is a layered bake of fried aubergine, tomato sauce, and cheese. Salting the aubergine first removes excess moisture so the slices fry rather than steam. The assembled dish needs 45 minutes in the oven and at least 15 minutes to rest before cutting.
Lay the aubergine slices in a colander in layers, sprinkling salt between each layer. Leave for 30 minutes. Rinse well under cold water and pat dry with kitchen paper.

Make the tomato sauce. Warm 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a saucepan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes, season with pepper, and simmer for 20 minutes until thick. Stir in the basil and set aside.

Heat a thin film of oil in the frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the aubergine slices in batches for 2 to 3 minutes each side until golden. Drain on kitchen paper. Top up the oil between batches.
Heat the oven to 200C. Spread a thin layer of tomato sauce on the base of the gratin dish.

Layer one third of the aubergine slices over the sauce. Add a layer of tomato sauce, then mozzarella, then a scattering of parmesan. Repeat the layers twice more, finishing with tomato sauce and a generous layer of parmesan.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until bubbling at the edges and the top is deep gold. Rest for 15 minutes before cutting.

items.symptom: The aubergine is oily and heavy.
items.cause: The slices were not salted or dried properly before frying.
items.fix: Salt for at least 30 minutes, then rinse and pat dry. Dry aubergine absorbs far less oil.

items.symptom: The layers break apart when serving.
items.cause: The dish was cut too soon after baking.
items.fix: Rest the parmigiana for at least 15 minutes out of the oven; the layers set as it cools slightly.

items.symptom: The top is pale and soft, not golden.
items.cause: The oven was not hot enough or the dish was on a low shelf.
items.fix: Place on the top shelf at 200C for the last 10 minutes, or switch to the grill briefly.
